components.name: pyside6_qt
components.note: PySide6-Essentials 6.11.2 (pinned >=6.8,<7 in pyproject.toml) bundles the Qt 6.11.2 libraries. The PyInstaller one-folder build links the Qt DLLs dynamically (they sit next to Spells.exe as separate files rather than being fused into one binary), so they remain independently replaceable per LGPLv3 section 4(d)/4(e). Paired with qt_licensing_notice below.

components.name: qt_licensing_notice
components.note: Copied from .venv/Lib/site-packages/pyside6_essentials-6.11.2.dist-info/METADATA (the wheel's own long description), which matches the upstream README verbatim. This is the notice PySide6 itself ships about being available under LGPLv3/GPLv2/GPLv3 or a commercial license, and it points to the Qt Licensing page.

components.name: portaudio
components.version: bundled with python-sounddevice 0.5.6 (not independently pinned; current PortAudio LICENSE.txt, latest tagged release v19.7.0)
components.note: sounddevice vendors prebuilt PortAudio DLLs under .venv/Lib/site-packages/_sounddevice_data/portaudio-binaries/ (libportaudio64bit.dll on Windows x64); the wheel does not record an exact upstream PortAudio version, so the license text is taken from the repository default branch.

components.name: numpy
components.note: Checked 2026-09-17: pip show numpy in .venv reports the package is not installed, and src/spells has no numpy import; neither sounddevice 0.5.6 nor PySide6-Essentials 6.11.2 pulls it in transitively in this build. Not currently shipped. Included for completeness per spec 21, and to re-check on future dependency changes.

components.name: pyinstaller_bootloader
components.note: Spec 19.3 step 5 packages the app with PyInstaller (one-folder build). The version is now pinned three ways at 6.22.3: build/pins.json toolchain.pyinstaller (the wheel plus its sha256), the pyproject dev extras, and the wheel installed in .venv by build/bootstrap_packaging.py. COPYING.txt was re-fetched at tag v6.22.3 on 2026-09-17 and is byte for byte the text already stored here, so the file and its sha256 are unchanged. It carries both the GPL terms and the Bootloader Exception in one file.

components.name: whisper_cpp

components.name: ggml

components.note: ggml is not a separate submodule at this pin; its source lives inside the whisper.cpp tree and is covered by the same 'The ggml authors' MIT copyright as whisper_cpp above.

components.name: llama_cpp
components.note: Pinned in build/pins.json binaries.llama_cpp_vulkan/llama_cpp_cpu. components.name: cpp_httplib
components.note: Vendored as a single header, build/cache/whisper.cpp-1.9.4/examples/server/httplib.h (CPPHTTPLIB_VERSION "0.20.0"), compiled into whisper-server.

components.name: nlohmann_json
components.note: Vendored as a single header, build/cache/whisper.cpp-1.9.4/examples/json.hpp (NLOHMANN_JSON_VERSION 3.11.2), compiled into whisper-server.

components.name: gcc_runtime_gplv3
components.note: Covers libgcc and libstdc++, statically linked into whisper-server.exe by build/build_whisper.py (-static, BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF). libgomp is statically linked too only when a static libgomp.a is present in the toolchain (build_whisper.openmp_args in build/build_whisper.py); otherwise the build falls back to GGML_OPENMP=OFF and ggml own thread pool, and libgomp is not linked at all. Paired with gcc_runtime_library_exception.

components.name: gcc_runtime_library_exception
components.note: The exception that lets a GPLv3-licensed runtime library be linked into a non-GPL binary such as whisper-server.exe; must ship alongside gcc_runtime_gplv3.

components.name: winpthreads
components.note: Statically linked into whisper-server.exe for -static builds. The mingw-w64 COPYING file itself carries both the project MIT notice and the BSD-3-Clause notice for the Lockless Inc. derived parts.

components.name: llvm_openmp
components.version: shipped inside the llama.cpp b10997 Windows release archives
components.note: libomp.dll ships beside llama-server.exe in both engine folders (build/build_whisper.py LLAMA_KEEP_DLLS); the zip already carries this exact license file, which build/build_whisper.py keeps because is_shipped_llama_file() allows any "license"-prefixed name.

components.name: whisper_model_weights
components.note: Covers the shipped ggml-large-v3-turbo-q8_0.bin. build/pins.json also pins ggml-tiny.bin (models.whisper_tiny_test) under the same MIT-licensed OpenAI Whisper weights, but that model is test-only (tests/integration/test_whisper_server_smoke.py) and is never staged into dist/Spells/models, so it does not get a separate shipped entry.

The benchmark picked Gemma 4 E2B for the default bundle (models.cleanup_model, B5-11), which is Apache-2.0 and needs no acceptance page; this Gemma Terms of Use text stays available in case a future Gemma 3 build ships, in which case spec 19.5 requires the Inno Setup installer to show it as a licence acceptance page and this entry's ships flag flips to true.

components.name: gemma4
components.version: Gemma 4 E2B (build/pins.json models.cleanup_model, data/models/catalog.json id gemma-4-e2b-it-q4_0)
components.note: Covers the shipped cleanup model gemma-4-E2B-it-Q4_0.gguf and its MTP draft head, upstream google/gemma-4-E2B-it, Apache-2.0 confirmed at https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/gemma_4_license. No installer acceptance page: spec 21 ties the page to the shipped model's catalog licence, and Gemma 4's is Apache-2.0, not the Gemma Terms of Use.

components.name: qwen3_asr

components.note: Speech model for English and German (spec 4, B5-13, B5-21, B5-26), upstream Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B. Neither ggml-org/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B-GGUF nor Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B carries its own LICENSE or NOTICE file, so the text is the canonical Apache License 2.0. The corrected speech rule (B5-26) now picks it alongside Whisper large-v3 turbo for the default English, German and Albanian selection on the processor, so build/package.py's default_bundle() ships it and the installer needs disk spanning (B5-27).
